sections.heading: Each {{entity_noun}} you identify qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: The record names the {{entity_noun}} in its own words about its subject — stated, not inferred. A named process or capability with no stated output identifies no {{entity_noun}}. Quote the words that name it.

children.text: Whose {{entity_noun}} it is has no bearing here. A candidate evidenced by another party's dealings is still identified and recorded.
A thing the record names as something else — a market, a credential, a machine, a material, a process — is that thing, not a {{entity_noun}}.

sections.heading: And every {{entity_noun}} you name must satisfy ALL of these:

rules.text: It is a determinate category: neither an individual item — one specimen, identified as itself rather than as a kind — nor a term so general it fixes nothing. A record naming a specific item is reported as the category that item belongs to.

children.text: A record that identifies one particular item — by a model designation, a catalogue reference, or any other mark that singles that one out — names an item rather than a category. Report the kind the record names that item as, and carry none of what singled it out into the category name; where the record names no kind for it, there is no category to report.
Where a record names something the manufacturer's output goes into, is fitted to, or serves, the category is that output itself, never the larger thing it becomes part of.

rules.text: It is distinct from every other {{entity_noun}} named for the same record. Two names for the same {{entity_noun}} in different words are one, not two.
